page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Tau T2A family. Powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, this instance provisions 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with a single thread per core. The memory configuration provides 8.0 GB of RAM, equating to 4.0 GB per core, backed by 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The server includes no bundled local storage and zero GPU accelerators.

Performance profiles reflect the balance of a dual-core ARM topology. Single-threaded evaluation displays stable compute capabilities, reaching an average bracket score of 1812.29 in stress-ng single-core tests and 24.01 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. In contrast, multi-threaded output is bounded by the small core count, recorded at a Geekbench multi-core score of 1997.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 1596.29. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 26.99 GB/sec alongside write bandwidth of 16.42 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput measures 2.66 GB/sec, while Redis SET performance achieves 2.61 million operations per second.

By delivering dedicated ARM physical cores without hyperthreading, the instance ensures consistent execution without sibling-thread contention. Its compact profile offers high resource efficiency for ARM-targeted workloads, making it appropriate for lightweight web serving, microservice containers, basic application staging, and general ARM64 software development.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARM architecture, powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. The configuration provides 2 dedicated physical cores, 2 vCPUs, and 8.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It includes no bundled local storage and no GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate solid single-threaded performance in lighter computational tasks, achieving an average rating in single-core stress-ng tests and gzip compression, though overall multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth fall into lower percentile brackets due to the modest core count. Operating without hyperthreading ensures predictable instruction execution. The instance delivers a resource-efficient footprint tailored for lightweight web serving, microservices, continuous integration tasks, and basic development or testing environments compiled for ARM64 platforms.
